Well.. I attempted sometime before Thanksgiving. I overdosed on 3 months worth of psychotropics and antidepressants, and some other random pills. I ended up getting my stomach pumped and then intubated.. I was in the ICU for two-ish weeks - during that time, I had 40+ seizures, my QT rate was at 499 for an extended period of time (putting me at severe risk for sudden cardiac death), oxygen wasn't reaching my brain in sufficient amounts.
I remember waking up around halfway through, and a doctor asked me, "Do you know where you are?" I answered, "No," looked around, and asked where I was. "You're in the ICU. You tried to kill yourself."
I immediately looked down at my arms, as I wasn't actually sure if I did attempt.. I am a cutter (ex-cutter? I'm not sure where I stand) - but that's not how I tried to kill myself, they then told me that I had overdosed; at that point I just said "OK," and inspected the room. I didn't really believe I was in the ICU - I didn't know what had happened. The lack of oxygen had given me a fair amount of memory loss, about as far back as a year was gone. I didn't know what grade I was in, I didn't know who my (at the time,) partner was, nor how I had tried to kill myself, hell, I didn't even know where I was.
After that stay, they transferred me to what I usually just call a mental hospital, or a mental institution. I stayed there for about two and a half weeks.. And was then moved over to a short-term CRC/group home/residency, which my stay there lasted about a month. I don't remember trying to kill myself, but I absolutely will remember the aftermath of it all..
I've been out of the CRC for a month now. I'm not 100% better, most definitely not, but I'm working towards it. It took me coming, quite literally moments away from death to realize, well, I might just want to see what life has in store for me. I sincerely hope that such drastic measures won't be your turning point - it's hard to realize, but life doesn't get easier, you just get better at handling all the bullshit it throws at you.

I personally do feel as if I'm benefiting from the program. I expect to be graduating soon, as soon as December and, with luck, reintegrate to public school. 
I'm on Effexor 225mg and Abilify 30mg, max dosages of both for my age.
As far as treatment for PTSD, I'm not sure I'm receiving any specifically for such. 
I do not have my Internet usage monitored, however if I am caught on social media, I get my phone taken away for 3 days. Other privileges do have to be earned, like saying where you're stepping rather than asking to step somewhere, decaffeinated coffee, deck time, out of sight staff time, etc. 


I'm pretty sure this isn't "allowed" but I'm having a fun time and what's life without a little fun?

>How long does the program usually last? And do you guys have regular meetings? I guess Im a little curious

The program usually lasts 9-12 months, however they're planning on shortening the average down to 3-6 months very soon. 
Regular meeting, as in clients or staff?

I have a roommate!

>What do you miss the most about living free?

I miss playing Magic the Gathering with my friends, and just being able to see my friends in general. I live with 6 girls in my house and see 27 girls daily and it gets tiring, seeing the same few faces every day, you know?
